name: Schedule shifts and fill sick calls
summary: A central staffing office fills each shift that opens up after the six-week schedule is posted: sick calls a few hours before a shift, known leaves and vacant lines, and requests for extra staff when acuity or census rises. Clerks confirm with the charge nurse that the shift must be filled, then phone or text part-time and casual staff in seniority order, offer overtime, ask for approval, call an agency or escalate to the administrator on call. The work is slow because calls go one at a time with response windows and collective agreement rules on seniority, hours and rest, and mistakes lead to grievances, pay errors or units working short.

baseline.org_archetype: A three-site Ontario community hospital corporation with about 4,900 employees, most of them unionized (ONA, OPSEU, CUPE, SEIU), and a central staffing office open about 16 hours a day using a staff scheduling and time-and-attendance system with phone, text and voicemail.
baseline.notes: Automated call-out apps were being piloted in some Canadian hospitals in this period; this file assumes clerks still phoned staff one at a time for most shifts.

trigger: An employee calls in sick or absent, a leave or vacant line leaves a hole in the posted schedule, or a unit asks for staff above its baseline plan.
end_state: The shift is filled and the replacement is recorded with a pay code, or the shift is covered by working short or closing beds, or the request is declined; any grievance, workload report or attendance follow-up is recorded.

volume.seasonality: Higher from December to March (influenza and respiratory illness), in summer vacation months when fewer part-time staff are available, and on long weekends.

evidence.note: Derived: about 3,500 shift-working staff at about 0.8 FTE each, times 15 to 19 days absent per year (14.7 days in 2021, 19 in 2022 for nurses and allied health), gives about 3,500 to 4,400 absence shifts a month; known vacancies and extra-staff requests add to this and some absences are not replaced. Agrees with the organisation file range.

surge.cause: Staff illness and isolation in respiratory season and COVID-19 waves

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate. Annual average absence for nurses and allied health rose from 14.7 days (2021) to 19 days (2022) and by 4.2 days for nurses from 2019 to 2020 (Statistics Canada); the waves themselves were shorter and sharper than the annual averages show.

Duties from the provincial staff scheduler job description and the centralized staffing office model. 20 clerks cover about 16 hours a day, 7 days a week; about 16.5 FTE of their time goes to filling vacancies; the rest goes to posting six-week schedules and payroll data, which this file does not walk.
The RN in charge of each unit on each shift confirms whether a vacancy must be filled and re-assigns patients when it is not. Spread across all units; FTE is the author's estimate of that time.

Patient care managers on all programs approve overtime and extra staff on weekdays and follow up absences under the attendance support program. Author's estimate of time on this process across about 30 program managers, expressed in the medicine manager role.
Clinical administrators cover evenings, nights and weekends and approve overtime, agency use, redeployment or bed closures. FTE is the author's estimate.
Patient flow coordinators block beds on the bed board when a unit cannot be staffed; rare. Author's estimate.

roles.title: HR business partner / labour relations advisor

evidence.note: Labour relations advisors handle grievances about shifts offered out of seniority order. Author's estimate.

systems.name: Email, telephone, pagers and wireless phones
Electronic bed board and patient flow dashboard
Hospital information system (electronic patient record with ADT, order entry, results, eMAR and clinical documentation)

steps.name: Receive absence call or staffing request
steps.description: The staffing clerk answers the staffing line or plays back voicemail from an employee calling in sick, or takes a request from a unit for extra staff, or picks up an unfilled line on the posted schedule. The clerk notes the employee, unit, shift, job class and reason, and sorts the case as a short-notice absence, a known vacancy or a request above the baseline staffing plan.

error.defect_description: Wrong shift, date or unit recorded for the absence.

next.condition: known vacancy on the posted schedule (leave, vacant line, education day)
unit asks for staff above the baseline plan (acuity, one-to-one observation, surge beds)

evidence.note: Clerk duties from the job description; the three sources of vacancies (illness, unfilled needs, acuity) from the pressbook. Shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Code the absence and check attendance flags
steps.description: The clerk opens the employee's schedule in the scheduling system, replaces the shift with an absence code (sick, family emergency, bereavement, WSIB), checks the sick-time balance and whether the absence triggers the attendance support threshold, and notes when the employee expects to return.

error.defect_description: Wrong absence or pay code, which later shows up as a pay error.

control.basis: Hospital attendance support program and sick leave plan rules in the collective agreements

evidence.note: Job description: inputs absence and pay codes and informs payroll. Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Charge nurse confirms whether to replace
steps.description: The clerk phones or pages the RN in charge of the unit, who looks at the census, expected admissions and discharges and patient acuity against the unit's staffing pattern, and decides whether the shift must be filled, can be covered by moving patients between the remaining staff, or needs a different job class.

error.defect_description: Census projected too low, so the unit is left short later in the shift.

next.condition: not replaced; workload absorbed on the unit

evidence.note: Projected census and staffing ratio check from the pressbook worked example. Share not replaced is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check float pool and redeployment
steps.description: The clerk looks in the scheduling system for float or resource-pool staff already booked for the shift, and for staff on overstaffed units who could be moved, and checks that they are oriented to the unit before assigning them.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of float pool coverage at a large community hospital.

steps.name: Build the eligible call list
steps.description: The clerk pulls the seniority list for the unit and job class and filters it to part-time and casual staff who submitted availability for that date, are under their commitment or hours cap, would not be on overtime, have twelve hours' rest since their last shift and are oriented to the unit.

error.defect_description: An eligible senior employee is left off the list or the hours count is wrong.

control.basis: Collective agreement order for offering additional shifts (regular part-time by seniority and availability, then casual, then full-time at overtime), hours equalization and minimum rest between shifts

evidence.note: Order of offering and equalization rules from the pressbook; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Call part-time and casual staff in seniority order
steps.description: The clerk phones or texts each person on the list in turn, leaves a message, and waits a set response window (for example five minutes when the shift starts within eight hours) before moving to the next name, logging each call and answer for grievance protection.

error.defect_description: A name is skipped or the response window is cut short, breaching the seniority order.

control.basis: Collective agreement order for offering additional shifts (regular part-time by seniority and availability, then casual, then full-time at overtime), hours equalization and minimum rest between shifts

next.condition: a part-time or casual employee accepts at straight time

evidence.note: Sequential calling took enough time that a scheduler filled only 12-20 relief shifts a day (Island Health); 5-minute response window example from an Ontario local appendix; Stevenson hospital staff made dozens of calls per shift. Acceptance share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Offer the shift as overtime
steps.description: When no one accepts at straight time, the clerk offers the shift at premium rates to full-time staff and to part-time staff who would go over their hours, again in seniority order, or asks staff on the shift before to stay over part of the shift.

control.basis: Collective agreement order for offering additional shifts (regular part-time by seniority and availability, then casual, then full-time at overtime), hours equalization and minimum rest between shifts

next.condition: accepted on a weekday day shift

evidence.note: Full-time staff are asked last because extra hours are overtime; 30% of nursing employees worked overtime in 2022. Split by time of day is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Manager approves the overtime
steps.description: On weekdays the clerk phones or emails the unit's patient care manager, who checks the overtime against the unit budget and whether another unit could lend staff, then approves or declines the premium shift.

control.basis: Hospital overtime pre-approval policy (budget holder approval for premium hours)

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common Ontario hospital practice.

steps.name: Administrator on call approves the overtime
steps.description: Outside office hours the clerk pages the clinical administrator on call, who weighs the overtime against staffing across the site that shift and approves or declines it by phone; the clerk records the approver's name.

control.basis: Hospital overtime pre-approval policy (administrator on call approves after hours)

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common Ontario hospital practice.

steps.name: Request agency staff or escalate
steps.description: If the unit is one where agency nurses are allowed (often critical care, emergency or maternity), the clerk phones or emails the contracted nursing agency with the shift, unit and skills needed; otherwise the clerk reports the unfilled shift to the administrator on call.

next.condition: escalated to the administrator on call

evidence.note: Author's estimate; agency use rose in Ontario hospitals in 2021-2022 but was limited by unit and budget.

steps.name: Agency confirms a nurse
steps.description: The nursing agency searches its roster for a nurse with the required experience and orientation to the hospital and calls back to confirm a name, or says no one is available for that shift.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of agency response times.

steps.name: Administrator on call decides how to cover
steps.description: The administrator on call reviews staffing across all units for the shift, then moves a nurse from a less busy unit, approves a unit to work short with adjusted assignments, or, when staffing is unsafe, closes or holds beds so the bed flow team stops sending admissions.

control.basis: Hospital safe staffing and staffing escalation policy: administrator decides redeployment, working short or bed closure

evidence.note: Author's estimate of escalation practice; shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Enter the replacement and notify the unit
steps.description: The clerk books the replacement into the shift in the scheduling system with the right pay code (straight time, overtime, redeployment or agency), updates the daily staffing sheet and phones the unit so the charge nurse knows who is coming.

error.defect_description: Wrong pay code (for example straight time instead of overtime), found when the timesheet is checked.

evidence.note: Job description: schedules adjustments in the computerized system and submits pay codes to payroll.

steps.name: Block beds on the bed board
steps.description: A patient flow coordinator marks the closed or held beds as unavailable on the electronic bed board, tells the emergency department and the admitting physicians, and sets a time to review whether the beds can reopen at the next shift.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Charge nurse redistributes the workload
steps.description: The RN in charge reassigns patients among the nurses on shift, takes a patient assignment personally if needed, asks for help with breaks from other units and documents the short staffing on the unit staffing record.

next.condition: a nurse files a workload report

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Post the known vacancy as an open shift
steps.description: For a vacancy known days or weeks ahead, the clerk posts the shift on the open-shift list (paper board or scheduling system) when the six-week schedule is posted or when the leave is approved, so eligible staff can sign up.

control.basis: Collective agreement order for offering additional shifts (regular part-time by seniority and availability, then casual, then full-time at overtime), hours equalization and minimum rest between shifts

evidence.note: Schedules posted 3-6 weeks ahead; vacancies after posting offered under the collective agreement.

steps.name: Nurse files a workload report
steps.description: After the shift a nurse who felt patient care was put at risk completes the union's professional responsibility workload report form, describing the staffing and patient acuity, and gives it to the manager.

control.basis: ONA hospital collective agreement professional responsibility workload process

evidence.note: Author's general knowledge of the ONA workload report process; frequency is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Manager approves extra staff above baseline
steps.description: The unit manager (or the administrator on call after hours) checks the reason for the extra-staff request, such as a patient needing one-to-one observation, high acuity or surge beds opened, against the staffing budget and approves or declines it.

control.basis: Hospital staffing budget and approval policy for staffing above the baseline plan

evidence.note: Pressbook: increases in patient acuity drive added staff. Approval share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Open shift waits for sign-up
steps.description: The posted shift stays on the open-shift list until an eligible employee signs up or the clerk starts calling within a few days of the shift date; the scheduling system shows who has requested it.

next.condition: still open near the shift date

evidence.note: Posted shifts at an Ontario community hospital had a 70% fill rate with an app; the author assumes a lower 50% self-sign-up rate for 2019-2022 paper and system postings.

steps.name: Charge nurse updates the assignment board
steps.description: Once told who is coming, the RN in charge adds the replacement to the patient assignment sheet and adjusts assignments if the replacement is from another unit or an agency and needs a lighter or familiar assignment.

next.condition: absence meets the attendance follow-up threshold
repeated vacancy in the same line

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Labour relations reviews a shift grievance
steps.description: An employee who was not offered a shift in seniority order files a grievance through the union; the labour relations advisor reviews the call log and seniority list, meets the union and settles, often by paying the missed shift.

control.basis: Collective agreement grievance procedure under the Ontario Labour Relations Act and hospital arbitration rules

evidence.note: Pressbook: daily staffing errors lead to individual grievances about denied shifts or overtime. Frequency is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Manager reviews the workload report
steps.description: The unit manager reads the workload report, discusses it with the nurse and the union representative at the next workload meeting, and records any changes to the staffing pattern or escalation.

control.basis: ONA hospital collective agreement professional responsibility workload process

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Manager follows up the absence
steps.description: The manager reviews the employee's absence record flagged by the staffing office, and if it crosses the attendance support threshold, meets the employee or asks for a medical note, or refers a longer absence to occupational health.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Manager raises a job requisition
steps.description: When the same line keeps going vacant because of a long leave or resignation, the manager completes a requisition in the HR system to post a permanent or temporary position.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Nobody accepts and the unit works short
exceptions.description: Straight-time and overtime offers fail, no agency nurse is available and no other unit can lend staff, so the charge nurse redistributes patients; about one in five such shifts leads to a workload report.

exceptions.name: Beds closed for lack of staff
exceptions.description: The administrator on call closes or holds beds for the shift so the unit is safe with the staff it has; the bed board is updated and admissions wait in the emergency department.

exceptions.name: Shift offered out of seniority order
exceptions.description: A senior part-time employee was skipped or not given the response window; the union grieves and the hospital usually pays the missed shift.

exceptions.name: Long absence referred to occupational health
exceptions.description: A sick call becomes a multi-week absence; the manager refers the employee to occupational health and the staffing office books replacements for every shift until a work status update arrives.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the vacancy being reported to the shift being filled or closed
benchmarks.population: Shift vacancies at an Ontario community hospital, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: most sick calls arrive a few hours before the shift (agreements ask for at least 4 hours' notice) and are filled or escalated before it starts; known vacancies posted weeks ahead take days. No published time-to-fill was found.

benchmarks.unit: shifts per scheduler per day with sequential phone call-out
benchmarks.population: Island Health, British Columbia, before automated call-out (about 2015)

evidence.note: Stated in the article.

benchmarks.unit: share of shifts posted through an app that were filled

evidence.note: Vendor-reported pilot result.

benchmarks.unit: days absent for illness or disability per employee
benchmarks.population: Nurses and allied health professionals, Canada

evidence.note: Statistics Canada Labour Force Survey.

pain_points.description: Calling staff one at a time with response windows takes most of the clerks' day; a scheduler could fill only about 12-20 shifts a day by phone.

evidence.note: Island Health and Stevenson hospital descriptions of manual call-out.

pain_points.description: Seniority, availability, hours-equalization and rest rules are applied by hand from lists; a slip leads to a grievance and a paid missed shift.

evidence.note: Pressbook on seniority, equitability and grievances.

pain_points.description: Overtime and agency use need a manager or administrator on call to approve, which adds waiting at the busiest times of day.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: When nobody can be found, the unit works short or beds close, which slows admissions from the emergency department.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; consistent with RN vacancies doubling from 2019 to 2021 (Statistics Canada).

sources.title: Staffing and Scheduling Provisions in a Collective Agreement (Hospital Unit Administration, chapter 3)
sources.supports: Typical Ontario hospital collective agreement rules: schedules posted 3 to 6 weeks ahead and 4 to 8 weeks long; additional shifts offered by seniority to regular part-time, then casual, then full-time at overtime; ONA cancellation notice 24 h part-time and 48 h full-time; sick calls ideally 4 h before shift; 12 h between shifts; example of a 5-minute response window before calling the next person (ONA and Grand River Hospital local appendix 2021-2023).

sources.title: Adjusting the Master Schedule Based on Unit Requirements (Hospital Unit Administration, chapter 3)
sources.supports: Unit clerk and charge nurse project census, apply staffing ratios, compare with booked staff and sick calls and add or cancel staff by collective agreement order; RN staffing reviewed 24-48 h ahead; seniority plus hours equalization rules; daily staffing errors lead to individual grievances.

sources.title: Introduction to Staff Scheduling (Hospital Unit Administration, chapter 3)
sources.supports: Centralized, decentralized and hybrid hospital staffing offices; scheduling clerks assigned to units working with unit managers; hospitals moving to automated call-out and scheduling apps.

sources.title: Provincial Job Description: (213) Staff Scheduler
sources.publisher: Saskatchewan Association of Health Organizations and health unions (working-for-health.ca)
sources.supports: Staff scheduler duties: maintain master rotation under collective agreements, call and schedule replacements for short-notice absences, adjust schedules in a computerized system, maintain seniority lists, post replacement lists, submit data and pay codes to payroll.

sources.title: Relief nurse scheduling improved using Vocantas
sources.supports: Island Health (BC): schedulers phoning staff one at a time filled about 12 to 20 relief shifts per day each; short-notice replacement often arranged at the last minute; 119 schedulers; after automated call-out some filled 40 a day.

sources.title: ShiftLink app fills shifts at Stevenson hospital
sources.supports: Ontario community hospital: staff previously made dozens of calls to fill a shift; app pilot from November 2017 reported a 70% fill rate for posted shifts, about three responses per post and an 82.5% reduction in call-outs.

sources.title: Nurses: Working harder, more hours amid increased labour shortage
sources.supports: Nurses and allied health professionals averaged 14.7 days absent for illness or disability in 2021 and 19 days in 2022; nurses had the largest increase of any occupation group from 2019 to 2020 (+4.2 days); 30.3% of nursing employees worked overtime in 2022, averaging 8.2 overtime hours a week; RN vacancies rose 117% from Q4 2019 to Q4 2021.

assumptions: One case is one shift vacancy. Building and posting the six-week master schedule (a batch job done per unit) is not walked step by step. Clerk hands-on time per vacancy is set to about 30-40 minutes so that 4,000 vacancies a month fit within the 20 staffing clerks in the organisation file, consistent with Island Health schedulers filling 12-20 shifts a day by phone; clerk time on schedule building and payroll data is outside this file.

The charge nurse is represented by the inpatient RN role (med_rn) and the approving manager by the medicine patient care manager role (med_manager), although the same steps happen on emergency, critical care, maternity, surgical and support-service units with their own managers.
Pay codes and time entries flow to payroll each pay period through the scheduling system; manager timecard approval belongs to the payroll process and is not included.

Shares of sick calls, known vacancies and extra-staff requests, the acceptance rates at each stage and all step times are the author's estimates unless a step cites a source; Ontario collective agreement rules come from a 2025 college textbook quoting a 2021-2023 local appendix and are assumed to match 2019-2022 practice.

The simulated median cycle time is a few hours, driven by short-notice sick calls; the 90th percentile of several days comes from known vacancies posted ahead and from attendance follow-ups and grievances that finish later.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage times 1.35). Agency invoices and overtime premiums are not labour cost in this file.
